title: On a rate-limited account, usage at 90% winds work down and 94% stops new work
why: A rate-limited account that runs out mid-work loses unsaved work; a gentle wind-down at 90% and a hard stop at 94% let work finish and hand off.
note: R43 (owner 13:48 CST Nov 11, relayed by the retrospective; plan 488eba6): "it might just be somehow local in my mac's coordinators handoffs and not on claude-settings anywhere but ya it was basically just that after usage hits 90% everything looks to gently wind down and 94% is a hard brake". Retrospective's reading, sent to the owner for correction: on an account with a 5-hour or weekly limit, at 90% no new lane or agent starts, and running work finishes and writes its handoff; at 94% every session stops new work; an account with no limit never brakes. A lane first measures whether a hook can read the percentages. Home: new decision usage-brake. This ruling lived only in a Mac coordinator's handoff, so it is a case for the handoff-ruling guard. Triage lookup 13:49: the page held no such ruling; item 169 cites the owner's Nov 1 17:56 CST ruling "no usage limit; a standing session runs until autocompact" (for the no-limit account).
source: owner 2026-11-11 13:48 CST, relayed by the retrospective session
